question: What fish-sampling evidence does Su et al. (2009) provide for the Las Piñas–Parañaque Lagoon, and can its fish list be assigned to LPPCHEA or treated as a checklist?
citation: Su, G. S., Martillano, K. J., Alcantara, T. P., Ragragio, E., De Jesus, J., Hallare, A., & Ramos, G. (2009). Assessing heavy metals in the waters, fish and macroinvertebrates in Manila Bay, Philippines. Journal of Applied Sciences in Environmental Sanitation, 4(3), 187–195.

sourceAccess.accessMethod: Reviewed the full-text article displayed on ResearchGate on 2026-11-20. The page identifies the PDF as author content uploaded by Glenn lo Sia Su on 2014-04-05 and says content may be subject to copyright. No local article copy was retained. The journal’s historical trisanita.org archive did not open; the current domain root displays unrelated content, so an original publisher-hosted copy and item-specific license were not verified.
sourceLocators: Article citation and publication details: Journal of Applied Sciences in Environmental Sanitation 4(3), pp. 187–195, September–December 2009.
Sampling method, water-point discussion, and fish locality limits: printed pp. 188–189; ResearchGate full-text lines 274–346.
Monthly fish catch summary and Table 2 taxa: printed pp. 190–191; ResearchGate full-text lines 557–708.
Fish table captions identify samples from Las Piñas–Parañaque Lagoon, Manila Bay, September–November 2007: printed pp. 192–193; ResearchGate full-text lines 747–750 and 1188–1190.

fieldSample.studyPurpose: Assessment of cadmium, chromium, and lead in lagoon water and aquatic organisms; not a comprehensive fish inventory.
fieldSample.captureLocalityAsReported: Coastal lagoon of Manila Bay; fish-table captions name Las Piñas–Parañaque Lagoon.
fieldSample.methodAsReported: A local fisherman caught fish and macroinvertebrates with a trawl net; the paper describes a bottom-trawl route from the north end of the lagoon southward and back to the north end. Identification was said to follow FishBase.
fieldSample.sampleUnitLimit: The paper states 14 fish and macroinvertebrate species/taxa overall and lists ten fish table entries plus four macroinvertebrate entries. It does not provide counts for each fish taxon or a full abundance/effort series.
fieldSample.coordinatesAsReported: The methods mention five water-sampling points and print one coordinate pair (14°29′06.4″ N, 120°59′18.4″ E). The text does not establish that pair as each point or as fish-capture coordinates; no fish point or track is derived.

sourceNameDiscrepancies.decision: Preserve the Table 2 spelling as a source label; do not infer which occurrence string is a typographic/OCR error without checking the page image and source specimens.
Preserve the Table 2 spelling as a source label; do not silently normalize the later prose form.

notReportedOrUnresolved: No fish voucher numbers, accession records, or independently reviewable specimen identifications are given.
No fish-by-station coordinates, capture track, municipality assignment, or fish-specific salinity measurement is reported.
No complete survey frame, abundance estimate, effort standardization, or taxon-specific count is provided.
The precise overlap, if any, between the trawl route and the legally delineated LPPCHEA/Ramsar boundary is unresolved.

sourceLineage.relationshipTo2001ERDBRamsarSummary: This is a separately dated 2007 heavy-metal field-sampling paper. No reviewed passage links its fish sample to the 2001 ERDB survey summarized by the Ramsar RIS. Do not use it as independent validation of the Ramsar list or merge the two samples.
sourceLineage.primarySourceAssessment: The paper reports its own fish collection and analytical methods, so it is a primary sampling paper for the 2007 sample. The public full-text copy is author-uploaded rather than a verified publisher copy; identification and reuse remain limited as described above.

rightsAndEvidenceDecision.decision: Retain the limited source-attributed sampling context and Table 2 name strings in internal research only. Do not reuse the article tables, figure/map, heavy-metal results, or species list in the public app without rights, taxonomy, and locality review.

nextActions: Inspect the 2013 Manila Bay lead-bioaccumulation follow-up paper for species names, sampling dates, locality wording, and whether it represents new fish collection or reuses the 2007 sample; do not count it as independent until lineage is established.
If an accessible publisher or author copy with page images is found, visually verify the two Table 2 name discrepancies before any taxonomic crosswalk.
Keep the broad lagoon sample distinct from LPPCHEA-protected-area records unless a map, station source, or specimen data establish the spatial relationship.
Continue the NCR source sweep across freshwater, brackish, marine, and wetland contexts; NCR and Luzon remain incomplete.

sources.supports: ResearchGate page identifies the full text as author content uploaded by Glenn lo Sia Su and reproduces the 2009 paper, methods, trawl sampling statement, monthly results, Table 2 fish labels, and Las Piñas–Parañaque Lagoon table-caption context.

CAS Source Index confirms the Journal of Applied Sciences in Environmental Sanitation title, serial identity, and its historical trisanita.org journal URL; it does not validate the article’s fish data.
EBSCO author search results list the article under the 2009 journal, volume 4, issue 3, page 187 bibliographic entry.
